title: Task Tracker
story: Your to-do list is a mess of sticky notes. You need a system where each task has a priority (Low to Urgent) and a done status. You want to see descriptions like "[URGENT] Submit report — INCOMPLETE" at a glance.
why: Enums make status and priority self-documenting — `Priority.Urgent` is clearer than a magic number like `4`.
analogy: Priority is like a traffic light for your tasks: Low is green (no rush), Medium is yellow (pay attention), High is red (act soon), and Urgent is flashing red (drop everything).
try_it: Add a `due_in_days: Int` field to Task. Write a function `is_overdue` that returns true if due_in_days is less than 0. Create your actual to-do list for today with 5 tasks at different priorities.
tips: Chain `if` statements for priority labels — start with the most common or most important case
Use `!t.done` to check if a task is NOT done — the `!` flips the boolean
Keep the describe function separate from the struct so you can change the format without changing the data
common_mistakes: Ordering priority checks backwards — if you check `Low` first, the else-if chain may not reach `Urgent`
Using a string for priority instead of the enum — you lose compiler safety
